name: LlamaIndex
pros: The right tool for document-centric RAG specifically
files: Loaders for PDFs, Word documents, spreadsheets, databases, and web pages.
value: The standard framework for connecting language models to private document stores. Where LangChain is more general-purpose, LlamaIndex is specifically optimized for the ingest-index-retrieve-generate pattern that makes RAG work well in practice.

reading.body:
LlamaIndex is the dominant open-source framework for retrieval-augmented generation over private document collections, purpose-built for the ingest-index-retrieve-generate pattern rather than general-purpose orchestration.

The framework itself contributes almost no latency and costs nothing to run. Latency is determined by the model and vector store the implementer chooses, and retrieval quality is determined by chunking strategy and embedding model selection. LlamaIndex supplies the connective tissue between loaders, indexes, and models, but every decision that affects output quality sits outside the framework.

The governance risk the data identifies is specific and serious. Whatever documents are fed into the index can be surfaced in model responses, and access control on the index is not enforced automatically. A team that indexes a shared drive without designing explicit access controls has, in effect, given every user of the system query access to every document the indexing process could reach. The framework does not prevent this, and the data notes it as the most common failure mode.

What the data does not cover is infrastructure footprint. LlamaIndex orchestrates calls to external models and vector stores, so the compute and storage costs of any deployment are entirely a function of those chosen components, not the framework itself.

tagline: The framework for building retrieval-augmented applications on top of your own documents.
use_cases: Building a knowledge assistant that answers questions from internal documents
Creating a retrieval layer that feeds context into a language model accurately
Ingesting heterogeneous sources (PDFs, databases, APIs) into a queryable index
integrations: Every major vector store and embedding provider
governance_note: The governance surface of a RAG system is the index, not the model. Whatever documents go in can come out in model responses, including documents that were accessible to the indexing process but should not be surfaced to end users. Access control on the index is not automatic and must be designed explicitly. The most common failure is indexing a shared drive and discovering that everyone can now query everyone else's sensitive files.
training_optout: Framework only. Data handling depends entirely on the model and store chosen.
